fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. Moses asked to see the LORD's glory, and the LORD answers by saying what He will do. First, “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you…” (Exodus 33:19). Then He says He will proclaim His name, the LORD, with Moses standing right there to hear it.

Nice try, friend, but this verse doesn't mention a pen or any writing. It says, “…the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). Moses goes in, the cloud comes down, and the LORD speaks with him. The verse gives us a conversation, nothing more.

Yes, baker! “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). That line is the heart of the scene. It's like two friends talking across the counter, with nobody in between. Right after it, Moses speaks to the LORD (Exodus 33:12), and the LORD answers him (Exodus 33:14).

Careful, baker, Moses isn't being sent off solo. The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). Notice who's doing the going: it's His own Presence. I think Moses was worried about who would go with him, since he says, “…You have not let me know whom You will send with me.” (Exodus 33:12). Walking a long road all by yourself sounds rough, and I bet he'd say so too.

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The passage does not say that nobody is writing in this scene. It also says the LORD spoke with Moses, not that only the LORD did the talking.
Exodus 33:12 records Moses speaking, but the LORD's answer comes in verse 14. The reference given does not cover both.
Moses's worry is stated as a fact rather than a guess. Papa Dorin also says he spent years alone in the drawer, but his backstory says he had companions there.
